title: WIP: Nubis-based volumetric clouds
abstract: > [!NOTE] > This is a working branch, not the final diff intended for upstream Bevy. It still contains debugging and validation features (shader debug defines, a reference path tracer, GPU timing and readback dumps, and environment-variable switches in the example) that would be removed or split out before a PR to `bevyengine/bevy` main. ## Summary Volumetric clouds for the atmosphere plugin, combining several published techniques: - **Atmosphere and lighting:** Hillaire 2020 (sky-view/aerial-perspective LUTs; its multiple-scattering transfer fraction, applied to clouds through a per-voxel escape probability). Frostbite (Hillaire 2016) energy-conserving integration and temporal reprojection. - **Physically based shaping (the default, `CloudProfiles::Physical`):** a parcel ensemble (Neggers, Köhler & Beljaars 2009) bakes, per air mass, the cloud fraction, in-cloud liquid water, cloud base and updraft speed against height. A statistical cloud scheme (Sommeria & Deardorff 1977) turns them into clouds; the details are below. - **Nubis shaping (`CloudProfiles::Nubis` / `Envelope`):** Nubis Evolved (Schneider 2022) dimensional profile and Perlin-Worley shape noise; Nubis Cubed (2023) alligator detail noise and distance-adaptive stepping. - **Multiple scattering in thick cloud:** a 3D delta-Eddington diffusion solve on the cloud field (similarity scaling after Joseph, Wiscombe & Weinman 1976), checked against a Monte Carlo of the IPRT C2 cube (Emde et al. 2019). - **Phase:** cloud droplet Mie phase from Jendersie & d'Eon 2023. - **Shadows:** UE5-style cloud shadow map (front depth, mean extinction, max optical depth), shared by the sky, ground and mesh lighting. Its centre is fixed while the sun turns, and its time-sliced history is trusted only as far as the light has turned since each texel was traced. - **Cirrus:** thin layers after Hogan & Kew 2005 (−5/3 fBm, log-normal ice water, fall streaks). ### Physically based shaping - **Air masses:** the profile rows span four LES cases, ordered by cloud-top height: - stratocumulus, DYCOMS-II RF01 (Stevens et al. 2005); - trade cumulus, BOMEX (Siebesma et al. 2003); - deeper trade cumulus, RICO (van Zanten et al. 2011); - continental cumulus, the CASS composite of ARM SGP (Zhang et al. 2017), validated against its LES and ARSCL profiles. - **Cloud base and lean per air mass:** each air mass has its own cloud base (its lifting condensation level). It also leans through the wind shear along the trajectory of its own updraft, so marine cumulus lean from low down and continental towers stand upright. - **Cloud detail:** clouds are a union of thermal bubbles over the coherent plumes, and their surfaces reach the measured fractal dimension 7/3 (Siebesma & Jonker 2000). - **Distance:** each sample stands for its pixel footprint, through the scheme's Gaussian closure, so detail stays physically consistent with distance. - **Liquid water:** a mixed shell at the cloud edge, after aircraft composites (Wang, Geerts & French 2009). - **Droplet number:** it sets the extinction per liquid water (Twomey; Martin, Johnson & Spice 1994), so maritime clouds are more translucent than continental ones. - **Weather:** - a per-view weather window around the camera carries art and physical channels (coverage, cloud type, cloud-fraction scale, air mass, droplet number); - world-anchored `CloudInfluence` entities edit it (masks and blend modes); - the cloud life cycle and wind advection move the field. API: - **Layers:** `VolumetricCloudLayer` and `ThinCloudLayer` as related entities of the atmosphere (`CloudLayerOf`), with an `AtmosphereWind` profile shared by all layers. - **Profiles:** `CloudProfiles` (physical, Nubis, envelope, or a custom lookup image). - **Weather edits:** `CloudInfluence`. - **Debug view:** `AtmosphereDebugViewPlugin` shows live previews of the LUTs, cloud buffers, cloud field, weather and noise; Tab in the example. ## References - S. Transfer, 2019. ## Showcase ## AI disclosure This PR builds on my earlier work and research on atmosphere and cloud rendering. It was produced partly with AI assistance (Grok 4.7 and Claude Opus 5.5), under my direction: - **Papers as the reference:** methods and constants come from the cited sources, with the papers and talks read directly. The aim is to derive physical quantities rather than fit them, with citations in the code. - **Visual iteration:** bugs (banding, crawling, holes, shadow seams) were reproduced at fixed camera poses, fixed, and checked with before/after screenshots. - **Measured feedback:** each change was checked against frame time (alternating A/B runs, per-pass GPU timings) and image regressions (pixel diffs against the previous build). Changes that did not pay off were reverted. - **Review:** an independent audit of the branch and its adversarial re-review guide the remaining fixes.
